def lex_min_assignment(n, allowed):
    """Assign n jobs to n workers, one job each, minimizing the assignment lexicographically.

    Workers and jobs are numbered 0..n-1.  allowed[i] is a list of distinct
    job numbers that worker i is qualified for (possibly empty, in no
    particular order).  A valid assignment is a list a of length n where
    a[i] is the job given to worker i, every a[i] is in allowed[i], and all
    a[i] are pairwise distinct (a perfect matching of workers to jobs).

    Return the valid assignment that is lexicographically smallest, as a
    list of n integers (minimize a[0]; among those, minimize a[1]; and so
    on).  If no valid assignment exists, return the empty list [].

    Constraints: 1 <= n <= 30; each allowed[i] is a list of distinct
    integers in the range [0, n).

    >>> lex_min_assignment(2, [[0, 1], [0]])
    [1, 0]
    >>> lex_min_assignment(3, [[0, 1, 2], [0, 2], [0]])
    [1, 2, 0]
    >>> lex_min_assignment(2, [[1], [1]])
    []
    """
